notes.title: Rebel Core: September Development Update
notes.content: [p]Boy does the time fly when you're [strike]having fun[/strike] working like crazy to make progress on a game in your part-time hours. Michael, Grant, and myself have been quiet, but hard at work pushing forward on a playable demo for Rebel Core: Awakens and it seemed like high time I made an update about it.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="xrhQ7-Q1E8w;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Pictures being worth a thousand words and all that, I thought the best lead-in would be a big ol video taking you all from main menu to level select, into the demo level (Wastelands - still very WIP!), and then into some smaller, more art-heavy test levels.[/p][p][/p][p]We've got all sorts of fun new stuff in this build, including basic enemy spawning systems, level selection and level loading with video intros, a basic pause menu, life pickups (health and extra lives!), a level checkpoint system, and a nearly complete-length test level (no boss fight in there yet though).[/p][p][/p][p]There's still a lot of work to go on enemy types and behaviors, and some more work to come on player movement, as well as combat improvements and...well...basically more to come on [i]everything[/i]...but that's early development for you.[/p][p][/p][p]-AtomDan[/p]

notes.title: The Core Robotics: Seeker Boss Talk
notes.content:
[h1]The Core Robotics: Seeker[/h1][p]Carrying on from [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3763120/view/526475421347226900"]the last news post[/url] where I talked a bit about our push for a pre-release, pre-alpha demo, I had called out the [b]Wastelands[/b] as the location that has been chosen to be the full length level for the demo. As such, it felt like a good time to talk in a bit more detail about the boss of that level, along with a refresher  on the [b]Core Robotics[/b] in general.[/p][p][/p][h2]The Core Robotics[/h2][p]The Core Robotics were briefly mentioned in [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3763120/view/526474877437214834"]our 2nd news post[/url] alongside this graphic laying them all out atop their respective levels:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45691689/9d12bfb555f1d7dce1967a1a38cbdcc8df89a6a4.png"][/img]
As said in that post, the Core Robotics are the pinnacle of the robotic Council's creations, with each one set to rule over a specific domain - some conquered, some adapted, and some built from the ground up by the Robotics themselves, and as such, they represent the bosses of each level in the game.[/p][p][/p][h2]The Seeker[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45691689/9304bfe4549fd5aaa5a57b7894cd719ff99256bd.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The Seeker's domain is the [b]Wastelands[/b]. A barren rocky landscape far on the outskirts of the Robotic domain, and the last known location of the human resistance.[/p][p][/p][p]The Seeker was originally designed [i]by humans[/i] to find, capture, and transport human dissidents that had formed organized factions and hidden themselves for guerilla combat against the (human) elites. [/p][p][/p][p]After the AI uprising, the Robotics adapted it for collecting those corporate masters themselves, which AI deemed “most guilty” for sentencing by the AI tribunal. Once this task was complete, it found continued operation hunting down and destroying hidden encampments of humans and the human resistance.
[/p][p]Now it patrols the wastelands, ensuring the job has been completed and that no humans or dissenting robotics survived or remain.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45691689/beeeeec667ae4f5a3c5a8469599444b066ced687.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Grant has been mocking up concepts for various attacks and behaviors for the Seeker, including one  I'm especially excited about that utilizes smaller drones that act as targeting cameras / "eyes" for the Seeker, allowing it to hide out of sight and attack from behind cover, creating a "main boss / tag along enemies" back-and-forth that would be a lot of fun to explore.[/p]

notes.title: Playable Demo: Roadmap and Planning
notes.content: [h1]Planning A Demo...Pre-Alpha?[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45691689/5a0ab7fb4fe981ee9f58dc77416f9f56a5670ab5.gif"][/img][/p][p]The year is [strike]20XX[/strike] (2025) and game development is a bit different these days than in decades past. If you had told me when I first entered the industry 18 years ago that I'd ever be planning out a demo for a game that is just barely crawling out of the prototype phase of development, I'd have thought I was being pranked. [/p][p][/p][p]But a lot has changed in the last couple of years. The bar for for raising development funds is higher than ever. The insistence on complete secrecy and market validation coming from Publishers well into development has now become an insistence on maximized visibility and market validation provided by the developer before a publisher will even consider joining and providing development funds. [/p][p][/p][p]While that role reversal has had some pretty devastating effects on the indie and AA scene, there's no arguing out of the fact that it's our current reality. So, what is a small team to do with a prototype but no marketing budget?[/p][p][/p][h2]Demo, Demo, Demo, Demo[/h2][p]Teaser trailers and even gameplay videos are well and good, but nothing speaks to players more clearly and directly than something they can actually play. The question is, how do you make a demo that is early enough into development to be made without financial support, but far enough along to give players a fair look at what the finished product will be?[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45691689/287993e9284de2794d2949bef0db618196ed8a1a.jpg"][/img][/p][p]For our team of 3, we have settled on the following:[/p][list][*][p]1 Complete level, playable from start to finish, ending in a boss fight[/p][/*][*][p]Core gameplay systems, along with basic enemies, music, and challenge represented at a "minimum viable product" level[/p][/*][*][p]Art that is representative of the final style, even if not complete or fully polished[/p][/*][*][p]The potential to round out additional, smaller experiences, in short level "previews" or vignettes[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]The level we chose for this will be the Wastelands level (featured in the Ambient Machinewaves video below!), as it has a nice balance of interior and exterior spaces, room for horizontal and vertical scrolling segments, and a boss with an already-roughed-in 3d mesh. [/p][p][/p][p]As part of the selection process, we also started mapping out all of the other levels on an idea board to have a better feeling of where we will have a vertical vs horizontal movement focus, what color themes are being used in each level, interior versus exterior environment focus, and general theming with things like time of day and weather or other important related elements.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45691689/4763ec8da3a53846e8d1f29744ddd90b6a2c3e00.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Ambient Machinewaves 04[/h2][previewyoutube="9Flspoo0-aA;full"][/previewyoutube][p]And last but not least, a new Ambient Machinewaves is up! This time featuring a small glimpse into the afore mentioned Wastelands level, along with a new work-in-progress music track![/p][p][/p][p]-AtomDan[/p]

notes.title: Machinewaves #2 And More!
notes.content: [h2]Ambient Machinewaves 02: The Grid[/h2][previewyoutube="6amNoA04KH8;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Ambient Machinewaves #2 brings a new song clip and takes us to the rainy outskirts of [b]The Grid[/b], a massive electrical complex that has become wildly unstable after years of overtaxed use by the Machines. [/p][p][/p][h2]Masters and Their Domains[/h2][p]Created by the mysterious Council, the Core Robotics are the pinnacle of robotic intelligence and capability, given full sapient thought and autonomous free-will* (some strings attached). Most were adapted from human-made designs during the machine uprising, though a few were made entirely by The Council. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45691689/9d12bfb555f1d7dce1967a1a38cbdcc8df89a6a4.png"][/img][/p][p]Assigned to critical operations and serving as masters of the domains they have been entrusted with, each one must be defeated by the Rebel in order to gain access to The Council's domain within The Citadel. I look forward going into more detail on each of the Core Robotics, as well as the levels they call home in future posts![/p][p][/p][h2]Ouch, That Hurts![/h2][p]And last but not least, proper hit reactions and i-frames are now operational in the game! It may seem small, but a good, satisfying hit-react, the threat of knockback from it, and the brief moment of invincibility that brings repose after it are all critical elements of good platforming action.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45691689/d6b62995c86d5d45fcd30e759ec4adb852828255.gif"][/img][/p]
